response.sql:
WITH sex_counts AS (
    SELECT CASE
               WHEN p.SEX IS NULL THEN '<missing>'
               WHEN TRIM(p.SEX) = '' THEN '<blank>'
               ELSE p.SEX
           END AS sex_group,
           COUNT(*) AS examined_count
    FROM Examination e
    JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID
    GROUP BY CASE
                 WHEN p.SEX IS NULL THEN '<missing>'
                 WHEN TRIM(p.SEX) = '' THEN '<blank>'
                 ELSE p.SEX
             END
), totals AS (
    SELECT SUM(examined_count) AS overall_total,
           AVG(1.0 * examined_count) AS per_sex_average
    FROM sex_counts
), above_average AS (
    SELECT sc.*,
           1.0 * sc.examined_count / t.overall_total AS share,
           t.per_sex_average
    FROM sex_counts sc
    CROSS JOIN totals t
    WHERE sc.examined_count > t.per_sex_average
)
SELECT 'sex' AS row_type,
       sex_group,
       examined_count AS total,
       1.0 * examined_count / t.overall_total AS share_of_overall,
       NULL AS average_amount_above_per_sex_average
FROM sex_counts
CROSS JOIN totals t
UNION ALL
SELECT 'above_average_combined',
       NULL,
       SUM(examined_count),
       AVG(share),
       AVG(examined_count - per_sex_average)
FROM above_average;

assumptions.assumption: Counts examination records per patient sex, so a patient with multiple examination rows contributes multiple times. Patients without any examination are excluded. Blank strings (including whitespace-only values) and NULL sex values are separate groups; the labels <blank> and <missing> distinguish them from recorded values.
